Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. stock traded at USD 50.16 on the NYSE on September 18, 2026, a decline of 0.791 percent from the previous close of USD 50.56. The same market snapshot placed the 52-week range at USD 46.74 to USD 70.05 and market capitalization at USD 6.17 billion.

The price stood USD 20.05 below the 52-week high and USD 3.42 above the 52-week low, placing the stock closer to the lower end of its annual range than to the upper end.

That positioning gives the market data a clear interpretation: the annual range, rather than a fresh operating figure, currently provides the most visible reference point for the security. The USD 6.17 billion market capitalization also shows the scale assigned to the listed partnership at the cited date.

Brookfield reported capital raised of USD 77 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while fee-related earnings reached USD 808 million, up 20 percent year over year, according to The Globe and Mail on September 21, 2026.

The comparison matters because the 20 percent increase in fee-related earnings was paired with a large capital-raising figure, while the quoted BIP market data showed a share price below its 52-week midpoint of USD 58.395. Brookfield's broader platform therefore supplied a quantified operating reference, but the listed infrastructure vehicle still traded below the midpoint of its annual price corridor on September 18, 2026.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. stock closed at USD 50.16 on September 18, 2026, with the primary listing on the NYSE. The dated market figures and the second-quarter 2026 operating context provide the clearest current framework for assessing the share price without adding an unsupported forecast.
